messages.subject: feedback to R through Shiny
parts:
Hi there,

I have seen a few different ways to see feedbacks work with shiny.. most noticibly in https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/ITFUwvYE-f8

I wanted to see what is the latest and best method for doing so. Concretely, here is what I want to do -

1 - Have an input variable on client, that maps to input$myInput (easy)
2 - When I change this input, change an output variable (which could be free form html/json/whatever) output$myOutput
3 - At this point, javascript on client side activates (say after you click myOutput 3 times), does some lookup and change input$myInput (shiny binding breaks!)
4 - Shiny now looks at the new value of input$myInput and provides a new output ouput$myOutput

Step 3 is where things get tricky. When I tried with simple experiments, shiny binding breaks and then we can no longer do step 4. There is a way I noticed somewhere where we could unbind all and then bind it all back. I also noticed that there are some new experimental features. What is the best way of going about this?

Thanks,

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: feedback to R through Shiny
parts: It depends on what kind of input myInput is, but most of the ones we ship with Shiny have update<InputType> functions, e.g. updateSelectInput, that you can access from within server.R (such as within an observe({...}) block). That should take the place of step #3.
